subject: Geography
sub_topic: Ocean upwelling — impact on fisheries and climate

concepts.name: Mechanism of Coastal Upwelling: Ekman Transport and Wind Forcing
key_dimensions: Role of Trade Winds and Coriolis Effect in driving surface water away from coast
Ekman Spiral and the 90-degree deflection rule — common UPSC trap on direction (left vs right hemisphere)
Distinction between upwelling-favorable vs downwelling-favorable wind directions
Why upwelling is stronger and more persistent on eastern boundaries of oceans than western boundaries

concepts.name: Eastern Boundary Upwelling Systems (EBUS): The 'Big Four'
key_dimensions: Four major EBUS: California, Humboldt (Peru), Canary, and Benguela Current systems
Why eastern boundaries — not western — host the world's most productive fisheries (cold, nutrient-rich water)
UPSC trap: Confusing current names with upwelling system names (e.g., Humboldt Current vs Peru Upwelling)
Disproportionate contribution to global fish catch despite covering <1% of ocean area

concepts.name: Equatorial Upwelling: Mechanism and Significance
key_dimensions: Divergence of surface water at the equator due to opposing Coriolis deflections in each hemisphere
Role of Trade Winds in sustaining the equatorial cold tongue in the Pacific
Distinction from coastal upwelling — open-ocean, wind-driven divergence vs Ekman transport against coast
Why equatorial upwelling in the Atlantic and Pacific differs in intensity and seasonal variability

concepts.name: Nutrient Upwelling and the Biological Pump
key_dimensions: Upwelling brings nitrates, phosphates, silicates from the aphotic zone to the photic zone
Phytoplankton bloom → zooplankton → fish: the trophic cascade enabled by upwelling
Biological pump: carbon sequestration role of upwelling-driven productivity — climate angle
UPSC trap: Upwelling brings nutrients UP but also brings CO2-rich deep water to surface, potentially releasing CO2 — dual climate role

concepts.name: Humboldt (Peru) Current Upwelling System and Anchovy Fisheries
key_dimensions: World's most productive single fishery system — Peruvian anchovy (anchoveta) dominance
Mechanism: Southeast Trade Winds + Coriolis deflection driving offshore Ekman transport
Collapse of anchovy fishery in 1972–73 linked to El Niño suppression of upwelling — policy lesson
Guano birds (boobies, cormorants) and marine mammals as indicators of upwelling health

concepts.name: El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) and Upwelling Suppression
key_dimensions: El Niño: Weakening of Trade Winds → warm water sloshes eastward → thermocline deepens → upwelling suppressed
Impact on Humboldt and California upwelling systems — fish stock collapse, seabird mortality
La Niña: Enhanced Trade Winds → stronger upwelling → higher productivity — asymmetric impacts
UPSC trap: El Niño warms eastern Pacific and cools western Pacific — opposite of normal conditions

concepts.name: Benguela Current Upwelling System: Unique Characteristics
key_dimensions: Located on the west coast of southern Africa — driven by Southeast Trade Winds
Supports sardine and anchovy fisheries; the 'Sardine Run' off KwaZulu-Natal coast
Occasional intrusion of warm Agulhas Current water disrupts upwelling — 'Benguela Niños'
UPSC trap: Benguela is a cold current despite being in a tropical/subtropical location — upwelling keeps it cold

concepts.name: Canary Current Upwelling System and West African Fisheries
key_dimensions: Drives productivity off Morocco, Mauritania, Senegal — one of Africa's most important fishing zones
Seasonal variability: upwelling strongest in winter-spring in northern sector, year-round in southern sector
Geopolitical angle: Foreign fishing fleets (EU, China) exploiting upwelling-rich EEZ waters of West Africa
Link to Saharan dust deposition — upwelling brings nutrients, dust also fertilizes ocean (iron fertilization)

concepts.name: California Current Upwelling System and North Pacific Fisheries
key_dimensions: Driven by North Pacific High pressure system and northerly winds along US west coast
Supports salmon, sardine, anchovy, and Dungeness crab fisheries
Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO) modulates upwelling intensity on decadal timescales — beyond ENSO
Ocean acidification concern: upwelled deep water is naturally more acidic — corrosive to shellfish larvae

concepts.name: Open-Ocean (Divergence) Upwelling vs. Coastal Upwelling: Comparison
key_dimensions: Coastal: Ekman transport perpendicular to coastline; Open-ocean: Ekman divergence at equator or cyclonic gyres
Intensity comparison: Coastal upwelling is more concentrated and intense; equatorial is more diffuse but vast
Examples of open-ocean divergence zones: equatorial Pacific cold tongue, Antarctic Divergence
UPSC trap: Not all upwelling is coastal — Antarctic Divergence is a major open-ocean upwelling zone

concepts.name: Antarctic (Southern Ocean) Upwelling and Global Thermohaline Circulation
key_dimensions: Southern Ocean is the largest upwelling zone globally — brings deep, nutrient and carbon-rich water to surface
Role in the global ocean conveyor belt: upwelling of North Atlantic Deep Water (NADW) in Southern Ocean
Krill-based food web: upwelling → phytoplankton → krill → whales, penguins, seals
Climate significance: Southern Ocean upwelling releases stored CO2 — major natural carbon source

concepts.name: Upwelling, Sea Surface Temperature (SST), and Regional Climate Modification
key_dimensions: Cold SST from upwelling suppresses convective rainfall — creates coastal deserts (Atacama, Namib, Sahara coast)
Thermal inversion and fog formation: cold upwelled water cools overlying air below dew point
Differential SST between ocean and land drives sea breezes and local circulation patterns
UPSC trap: Atacama Desert aridity is multi-causal — upwelling + Andes rain shadow + subtropical high — not upwelling alone

concepts.name: Upwelling and Coastal Desert Formation: Atacama and Namib Case Studies
key_dimensions: Atacama (South America): Humboldt Current upwelling + cold SST suppresses precipitation — hyperarid
Namib (Africa): Benguela Current upwelling creates similar aridity on African west coast
Fog oases: Coastal fog (camanchaca in Atacama) as a moisture source for unique biodiversity
UPSC comparison trap: Both deserts are on western coasts, both linked to cold current upwelling — identify correct current for each

concepts.name: Upwelling and Ocean Acidification: The Compounding Threat
key_dimensions: Deep water upwelled is naturally high in CO2 and low in pH due to biological decomposition at depth
Anthropogenic CO2 absorption making upwelled water even more corrosive — 'double acidification'
Impact on calcifying organisms: pteropods, oysters, mussels — shells dissolve in corrosive upwelled water
California/Oregon coast as ground zero — oyster hatchery failures documented since 2000s

concepts.name: Upwelling and Oxygen Minimum Zones (OMZs)
key_dimensions: High productivity from upwelling → large organic matter sinking → bacterial decomposition consumes oxygen
OMZs expand below upwelling zones (e.g., Eastern Tropical Pacific, Arabian Sea) — hypoxic dead zones
Impact on demersal fish and benthic organisms — vertical habitat compression
Climate change expanding OMZs — interaction with upwelling intensity changes fishery productivity

concepts.name: Indian Ocean Upwelling: Monsoon-Driven Seasonality
key_dimensions: Unique system: Indian Ocean upwelling is seasonally reversing — driven by monsoon wind reversal, not steady Trade Winds
Southwest Monsoon drives coastal upwelling off Somalia (Somali Current reversal) and Oman/Kerala coasts
Somalia upwelling: one of the most intense in the world during SW Monsoon — cold SST in an otherwise warm ocean
UPSC trap: Indian Ocean lacks a permanent EBUS because monsoon reversal prevents year-round upwelling — unlike Pacific/Atlantic

concepts.name: Kerala–Karnataka Coast Upwelling and India's Fisheries
key_dimensions: SW Monsoon winds drive offshore Ekman transport along India's southwest coast — seasonal upwelling
Supports sardine, mackerel, and tuna fisheries — economically vital for Kerala and Karnataka fishing communities
'Oil sardine' (Sardinella longiceps) abundance directly correlated with upwelling intensity
Climate change concern: Studies show weakening/shifting of upwelling off Kerala affecting fishery yields

concepts.name: Climate Change Impacts on Global Upwelling Systems
key_dimensions: Bakun Hypothesis (1990): Global warming intensifies land-sea temperature gradient → stronger Trade Winds → stronger upwelling (counterintuitive)
Counter-argument: Stratification increases with warming → even if winds strengthen, upwelling brings less nutrient-rich water
Poleward shift of wind systems may shift upwelling zones away from productive areas
UPSC trap: Climate change impact on upwelling is NOT straightforwardly negative — it's a contested, nuanced area with competing hypotheses

concepts.name: Upwelling vs. Downwelling: Contrasting Oceanographic and Ecological Roles
key_dimensions: Downwelling: Convergence of surface water, water sinks, carries oxygen to depth but removes nutrients from surface
Western boundary currents (Gulf Stream, Kuroshio) associated with downwelling — nutrient-poor, less productive
Downwelling role in thermohaline circulation: NADW formation in North Atlantic — climate regulation
UPSC trap: Western Pacific/Atlantic (downwelling zones) are LESS productive than eastern boundaries (upwelling zones) — directly opposite intuition

concepts.name: Fisheries Management and the Upwelling-Overfishing Nexus
key_dimensions: Maximum Sustainable Yield (MSY) concept stressed when upwelling variability (ENSO) interacts with overfishing
Peru anchovy collapse (1972): ENSO + overfishing combination — which factor was primary? Policy debate
Ecosystem-based fisheries management (EBFM) needed in upwelling systems due to high natural variability
UPSC current affairs link: IUU (Illegal, Unreported, Unregulated) fishing concentrated in upwelling-rich EEZs of developing nations
